newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan premier's approval rate sinks to new low.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan premier's approval rate sinks to new low.

text.p: Taiwan Premier Lien Chan's approval rating has sunk to a new low at a time of growing dissatisfaction with violent crime, a newspaper poll published on Tuesday said.
Only 24 percent of the 762 people interviewed by the United Daily News on Monday said they were satisfied with Lien's performance, down six percentage points from a similar poll taken a week ago.
Around 50 percent said they were not satisfied with Lien's work, compared with 46 percent a week earlier, the poll showed.
Some 35 percent said the premier should step down to take responsibility for the island's deteriorating law and order, while 45 percent said he should stay.
Lien as premier is head of the administration and directly responsible for domestic affairs.

Taiwanese were shocked by last week's discovery of the body of 17-year-old Pai Hsien-yen, daughter of actress Pai Ping-ping. Her kidnappers, who dumped her naked body in a river, have not been caught.
More than 50,000 people outraged by the murder demonstrated on Sunday to demand the resignation of Lien and a cabinet reshuffle.
About 40 Taiwan students staged a protest in front of the island's cabinet building on Monday to protest at the worsening crime levels and ask Lien to take responsibility.
President Lee Teng-hui on Friday apologised for "worsening social law and order" and said his government would take full responsibility.
The United Daily News poll showed Lee's approval rate remained at 48 percent, unchanged from a week ago.
